question: Will another European country formally ban or enact equivalent restrictions on smart glasses (following Norway's regulatory move) before the end of 2026?

model.prompt_context:
Resolution criteria:
- "Yes": Wins if at least one European country (other than Norway) formally enacts — through legislation, a legally binding regulatory order, or equivalent government decree — a ban or equivalent use restrictions on smart glasses (i.e., camera-enabled wearable eyewear) strictly after 2026-10-01T18:07:36.389Z and at or before 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z. The measure must have legal force (proposals, consultations, expert-group appointments, and non-binding government guidance do not qualify).
- "No": Wins if no such formal, legally binding ban or equivalent restriction on smart glasses is enacted by any European country (other than Norway) strictly after 2026-10-01T18:07:36.389Z and at or before 2027-01-01T00:00:00.000Z.

Clarifications:
- "European country" means any sovereign state that is a member of the Council of Europe, the European Union, or the European Economic Area, excluding Norway.
- "Equivalent restrictions" means a legally binding prohibition or material limitation on the use, sale, or public operation of smart glasses — comparable in scope to a formal ban — enacted by a national government or its authorised regulatory body; voluntary retailer withdrawals, institutional workplace policies, and municipal-level rules do not qualify.
- Norway's "regulatory move" refers to the Norwegian government's announced plans (from August–September 2026) to regulate smart glasses, including potential bans on features such as facial recognition in public spaces; because Norway has not yet enacted a formal ban as of the window start, "another European country" must be a country other than Norway regardless of whether Norway ultimately enacts its own ban within the window.
